mathgap.title: Sequential processing of transfers
mathgap.principle: When a transfer statement appears, immediately adjust the giver's and receiver's counts before processing subsequent statements. This ensures later statements see the updated counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement of the form "X gives K items to Y" is encountered.
mathgap.example: Adding K to Y without subtracting K from X, leaving X unchanged.

mathgap.title: Signed difference equality
mathgap.principle: Translate statements of the form "the number of items that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of items that C and D have" into the equation (A − B) = (C − D), preserving the order of names on each side.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a comparison‑transfer statement that mentions "more than" on both sides.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "A has more than B" as |A − B| or swapping C and D on the right‑hand side.

mathgap.title: Direct count assignment at point of mention
mathgap.principle: When a statement directly gives a count, set the person's current count to that number at that moment, before any later transfers or updates.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a statement like "Person has N items".
mathgap.example: Assuming the count is final after all later transfers, ignoring subsequent changes.

mathgap.title: Update both parties in a transfer
mathgap.principle: For a transfer "X gives K items to Y", subtract K from X's current count and add K to Y's current count.
mathgap.example: Only adding K to Y while leaving X unchanged.

mathgap.title: Accumulate net change for multiple transfers
mathgap.principle: If a person appears in several transfer statements, sum all gains and losses to compute their net change, ensuring the final count reflects every transfer.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a person participates in more than one transfer statement.
mathgap.example: Counting only the first transfer and ignoring later ones.

mathgap.title: Systematic linear solving
mathgap.principle: After translating all statements into linear equations, solve the system using substitution or elimination to find each person's count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After extracting all constraints and before producing the final answer.
mathgap.example: Leaving equations unsolved and guessing the answer.

mathgap.title: Non‑negative integer check
mathgap.principle: All derived counts must be non‑negative integers; if any equation yields a negative or fractional value, the solution is invalid and a mistake has been made.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After solving the system, before committing to the final answer.
mathgap.example: Accepting a fractional count as a valid solution.

mathgap.title: Multiplicative update handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says a person's count "increases by K times" (or by a fractional factor), multiply the current count by that factor instead of adding it.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering statements like "X's count increases by 2 times" or "by 3/2 times".
mathgap.example: Treating "increase by 2 times" as adding 2 rather than doubling the count.

mathgap.title: Split operation handling
mathgap.principle: When a person splits all their items equally among two recipients, set the giver's count to zero and give each recipient half of the original amount (assuming integer division).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering statements like "X splits all the items she owns equally among Y and Z".
mathgap.example: Giving each recipient the full original amount and leaving the giver unchanged.

mathgap.title: Conditional transfer handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement includes a condition (e.g., "If X has more than N items, X will transfer their items to Y"), evaluate the condition based on X's current count at that point; if true, move all of X's items to Y (X becomes 0, Y gains the amount).
mathgap.example: Executing the transfer regardless of whether the condition holds true.

mathgap.description: Treating signed difference statements as absolute differences
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model often interprets "A has more than B" as a magnitude without regard to sign, ignoring that the order matters.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Translate such statements into signed equations (A − B) = ... preserving the order of names on both sides.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the sequential order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may treat all transfers as simultaneous, missing that later statements depend on updated counts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process each transfer in the order it appears, updating counts immediately before handling subsequent statements.

mathgap.description: Assuming explicit counts are final after all transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may think a direct count assignment overrides any later changes.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat explicit counts as setting the current count at that point; later transfers can modify it.

mathgap.description: Updating only the receiver in a transfer
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may forget to subtract the transferred amount from the giver.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When processing a transfer, subtract the amount from the giver and add it to the receiver.

mathgap.description: Reversing the direction in "X has N more than Y" statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may misinterpret "X has N more than Y" as Y − X = N.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret "X has N more than Y" as X − Y = N.
